result: In a large ME/CFS cohort, serum activin A and IL-21 (but not CXCL13) were raised and correlated with anti-EBV/HHV-6 dUTPase seropositivity; ME/CFS serum drove TFH differentiation via activin A, and viral dUTPases induced activin A in vitro and marginal-zone B/NKTFH cells in mice.
reason: Same anti-dUTPase serology, adds a downstream germinal-centre mechanism; likely same lab, so not independent.

result: In 128 post-COVID patients followed 12 months, cognitive impairment rose from 16% to 26%, and kynurenine, quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid were associated with cognitive decline (p<.001).
reason: Long COVID version of blood kynurenine pathway activation; within-patient association with cognition, no uninfected control comparison of levels.

result: 282 post-COVID patients scored lower than 52 matched controls on delayed verbal memory (r=.13), attention (r=.1) and executive function (r=.1) on OCS-Plus, with 10-20% more than 1.5 SD below control mean; fatigue, age and initial severity predicted performance.
reason: Long COVID version of attention/memory deficits; effects small and on a screening battery, not processing speed or reaction time.

result: In 60 LIINC participants at median 17.6 months, 18/37 (49%) with cardiopulmonary symptoms had reduced peak VO2 on CPET, chronotropic incompetence was the most common abnormality, and reduced capacity was associated with early elevated inflammatory markers.
reason: Same CPET measure and chronotropic-incompetence pattern in LC, adds link to early inflammation; possibly overlaps the Durstenfeld group already cited (authors not in file to confirm).

result: In 144 post-COVID subjects vs 144 propensity-matched controls at about 14 weeks, percent-predicted peak VO2 was lower only after severe COVID (72.2% vs 98.5% mild and 91.6% controls); limitation was attributed to peripheral muscle in 91.7%, with ventilatory equivalents, OUES and O2 pulse similar.
reason: Unselected post-COVID (41% symptomatic), only the severe subgroup is reduced, so not a replication; supports the peripheral-not-cardiac pattern and severity heterogeneity. Conference abstract.

result: Three-level meta-analysis of 15 studies (306 ME/CFS or FM patients, 292 controls) found higher post-exercise pain in patients (Hedges d=0.42, 95% CI 0.16-0.67), larger at 8-72 h (d=0.71) than at 0-2 h (d=0.32).
reason: Measures post-exercise pain worsening, which matches the exercise-hyperalgesia finding; the delayed-timing moderator secondarily supports PEM timing. Pools ME/CFS with FM.

result: 155 long COVID patients had reduced global HRV, lower parasympathetic and higher sympathetic modulation than 94 COVID-free controls on short-term HRV.
reason: Same HRV measure and direction but in long COVID, not an ME/CFS cohort, so extends rather than replicates.

result: 155 long COVID patients had reduced global HRV, lower parasympathetic and higher sympathetic modulation than 94 COVID-free controls on short-term HRV.
reason: Resting short-term HRV is not orthostatic testing (OH/POTS) or MSNA; the paper is covered by the neuro-hrv link.

result: In 148 CFS patients followed 6 months with weekly remote heart monitoring, non-improvers (n=92) had lower HRV than improvers (n=38; difference 5.93 ms, p=.032), while activity patterns including push-crash and pacing did not differ.
reason: Same HRV measure, adds prognostic/illness-trajectory dimension within ME/CFS.

result: In UK primary care records (2,130 Lyme vs 8,510 matched), Lyme disease was followed by more fatigue (seasonal HR up to 3.14) and ME/CFS diagnosis (11.76 vs 1.20 per 10,000 person-years; adjusted HR 16.95, 5.17-55.60; 17 events), attenuated but persisting after 6 months.
reason: Registry design showing strong enrichment of ME/CFS after a bacterial infection, which cuts against the viral-not-bacterial specificity claim; few events and possible coding bias.
